grh_4ac0b286aecf81b9a788.title: Mrs Mike
paragraphs: Boston-raised Kathy O'Fallon marries Mountie Sergeant Mike Flanagan and follows him into the isolated Canadian North, where she must learn to live with brutal cold, cultural differences, scarce supplies and Mike's responsibility for everyone in his enormous district. The hardships gradually become part of their shared life until an epidemic sweeps the settlement. Despite Mike's efforts and the eventual arrival of serum, their baby dies, and Kathy, overwhelmed by grief, decides she cannot survive the North and leaves. Mike transfers back to his old post believing he has lost her. Kathy ultimately turns back after seeing another frontier family recover from the loss of a child, telling Mike that they cannot let the North defeat them and that, together, they will keep fighting it.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Martha Wentworth, Byron Kane, Evelyn Keyes, Louis King, and Hal Girard. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Howard Wiley as producer, Richard Allen Simmons as radio adaptor, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 60 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]] and [[org|org.50075df24f7e1a61|Anacin]].

This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.dfbb6b50dd1841a4|Mrs Mike]]. Benedict Freedman is credited as author, Nancy Freedman is credited as author, and Richard Allen Simmons adapted it for radio.

grh_4a59dffb8208056de9d8.title: Bad Boy
paragraphs: Fifteen-year-old Ted Gallagher is caught with a gang after a nighttime jewelry-store break-in in which the watchman is shot. The town is ready to write Ted off as a bad boy, but Dr. Christian argues that the neglected youngster has never been given a fair chance. Judge Latimer places Ted on six months' probation under the doctor's supervision instead of sending him to reform school. Ted begins to flourish, showing unexpected skill caring for injured animals and an interest in medicine. Then, just before a birthday party arranged for him, Ted gets into a school fight with Buddy Melrose and Buddy dies. Ted admits striking him but refuses to explain the quarrel. Dr. Christian proves that Buddy had a congenital blood-vessel defect and suffered the fatal rupture before Ted's blow landed, clearing Ted of responsibility. A notebook finally reveals why Ted kept silent: Buddy had written a mocking poem about Dr. Christian, and Ted fought to defend the man who had believed in him.

The cast includes Rosemary De Camp, Bobby Mauch, Albert Van Antwerp, Jean Hersholt, and Joe Forte. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_4a22b1b936691972f05d.title: The Adventure of the Uneasy Chair
paragraphs: Harriet Ervin asks Holmes to clear her fiancé, secretary Robert Binion, after her father Sir Edward is found dead in a locked study while Binion sat outside. A constable later dies in the same chair while Binion is jailed, apparently proving his innocence. Holmes discovers that the antique chair is one of a pair and contains a concealed spring that can drive a needle into the sitter's brain; someone had switched the identifying cord so the lethal chair was delivered to Sir Edward. The apparent exoneration was the murderer's design. Holmes replaces the fatal chair with its harmless twin and sits in it before the suspects. Binion alone panics, exposing that he engineered the chair murders and the evidence trail so a clever investigation would clear him.

[[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce. Other credited names include Edna Best as producer, Denis Green as writer, Anthony Boucher as writer, and Harry Bartell as announcer.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.001bd720d2ad4e68|The Musgrave Ritual]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.
